title_en: Measures for the Registration of Mineral Resource Mining

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Measures are formulated in accordance with the Mineral Resources Law of the People's Republic of China for the purposes of strengthening the administration of mineral resources exploitation, protecting the lawful rights and interests of mining right holders, maintaining the order of mineral resources exploitation, and promoting the development of the mining industry.
Article 2 Any person who exploits mineral resources within the territory of the People's Republic of China and other sea areas under its jurisdiction must comply with these Measures.

Article 4 Before filing an application for a mining right, the applicant for a mining right shall, on the basis of the approved geological exploration reserve report, apply to the registration authority for delineation of the mining area.
If it is necessary to apply for project approval and establish a mining enterprise, the applicant shall, on the basis of the delineated mining area, handle the relevant procedures in accordance with state provisions.

Article 6 The registration authority shall, within 40 days from the date of receipt of the application, make a decision on whether to grant registration or not, and shall notify the applicant for a mining right.
If the applicant for a mining right is required to modify or supplement the documents prescribed in Article 5 of these Measures, the registration authority shall notify the applicant for a mining right to make the modification or supplement within a specified time limit.
If registration is granted, the applicant for a mining right shall, within 30 days from the date of receipt of the notice, pay the mining right usage fee in accordance with Article 9 of these Measures, and pay the consideration for the mining right formed by state-funded exploration in accordance with Article 10 of these Measures, go through the registration procedures, obtain the mining license, and become a mining right holder.
If registration is not granted, the registration authority shall state the reasons to the applicant for a mining right.

Article 7 The term of validity of a mining license shall be determined according to the construction scale of the mine: for mines above large-scale, the maximum term of validity of the mining license is 30 years; for medium-scale mines, the maximum term is 20 years; for small-scale mines, the maximum term is 10 years. If it is necessary to continue mining after the expiration of the term of validity of the mining license, the mining right holder shall, within 30 days prior to the expiration of the term of validity of the mining license, go through the renewal registration procedures with the registration authority.
If the mining right holder fails to go through the renewal registration procedures within the prescribed time limit, the mining license shall automatically become null and void.

Article 8 After issuing a mining license, the registration authority shall notify the relevant county people's government in the locality of the mining area. The relevant county people's government shall, within 90 days from the date of receipt of the notice, make a public announcement of the mining area, and may, at the request of the mining right holder, organize the erection of boundary pillars or the installation of surface markers.

Article 9 The state implements a system of compensated acquisition of mining rights. The mining right usage fee shall be paid annually according to the area of the mining area, at a rate of 1,000 yuan per square kilometer per year.

Article 10 If applying for a mining right in a mineral deposit that has been explored and verified with state-funded exploration, the applicant for a mining right shall, in addition to paying the mining right usage fee in accordance with Article 9 of these Measures, also pay the consideration for the mining right formed by state-funded exploration; the consideration for the mining right may be paid in a lump sum or in installments in accordance with relevant state provisions.
The consideration for the mining right formed by state-funded exploration shall be appraised by an appraisal institution with the qualification for mining rights appraisal; the appraisal report shall be submitted to the registration authority for record.

Article 11 The mining right usage fee and the consideration for the mining right formed by state-funded exploration shall be collected by the registration authority and shall all be included in the state budget management. The specific measures for management and use shall be formulated by the competent geology and mineral resources department of the State Council jointly with the finance department and the planning department of the State Council.

Article 13 Mining rights may be acquired through public bidding in a compensated manner.
The registration authority shall, in accordance with the authority prescribed in Article 3 of these Measures, determine the mining area for bidding, issue a bidding announcement, and set forth bidding requirements and the deadline; however, the mining area for bidding to foreign parties shall be determined by the competent geology and mineral resources department of the State Council.
The registration authority shall organize bid evaluation and select the winning bidder on the principle of selecting the best. After paying the fees prescribed in Articles 9 and 10 of these Measures, the winning bidder shall go through the registration procedures, obtain the mining license, become a mining right holder, and fulfill the obligations undertaken in the bid.

Article 14 The registration authority shall, according to law, supervise and inspect the mining right holders within its administrative region with respect to their rational development and utilization of mineral resources, environmental protection, and other legal obligations that they shall perform. The mining right holders shall truthfully report relevant information and submit annual reports.

Article 16 If a mining right holder suspends operations or closes a mine during the term of validity of the mining license or upon its expiration, it shall, within 30 days from the date of the decision to suspend operations or close the mine, apply to the original licensing authority for cancellation registration of the mining license.

Article 17 If any unit or individual engages in mining without obtaining a mining license, or enters a state-planned mining area or a mining area of significant value to the national economy for mining without authorization, or exploits specific mineral species subject to protective exploitation as prescribed by the state without authorization, or mines beyond the approved mining area, the registration authority shall impose penalties in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 18 If any person fails to submit an annual report in accordance with these Measures, refuses to accept supervision and inspection, or practices fraud, the department responsible for geology and mineral resources management of the people's government at or above the county level shall, within the authority prescribed by the competent geology and mineral resources department of the State Council, order cessation of the illegal act, issue a warning, and may also impose a fine of not more than 50,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the original licensing authority shall revoke the mining license.

Article 19 If any person damages or removes without authorization boundary pillars or surface markers of a mining area, the department responsible for geology and mineral resources management of the people's government at or above the county level shall, within the authority prescribed by the competent geology and mineral resources department of the State Council, order restoration within a time limit; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not more than 30,000 yuan shall be imposed.

Article 20 If any person prints without authorization, forges, or fraudulently uses a mining license, the department responsible for geology and mineral resources management of the people's government at or above the county level shall, within the authority prescribed by the competent geology and mineral resources department of the State Council, confiscate the illegal gains, and may also impose a fine of not more than 100,000 yuan; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 21 Whoever, in violation of these Measures, fails to pay the fees as prescribed by these Measures within the prescribed time limit, the registration authority shall order them to pay within a specified period, and shall impose a late payment fee of 2‰ per day from the date of delay; if they still fail to pay after the expiration of the specified period, the original issuing authority shall revoke the mining license.

Article 22 Whoever, in violation of these Measures, fails to go through the formalities for alteration registration or cancellation registration of the mining license, the registration authority shall order them to make corrections within a specified period; if they fail to make corrections within the specified period, the original issuing authority shall revoke the mining license.

Article 23 Whoever, in violation of these Measures, exploits petroleum or natural gas mineral resources, the competent geology and mineral resources authority under the State Council shall impose an administrative penalty in accordance with the relevant provisions of these Measures.
Article 24 Where the mining right holder's mining license is revoked, it shall not apply for a mining right again within two years from the date of revocation of the mining license.

Article 25 Where any staff member of the registration authority engages in malpractice for personal gain, abuses power, or neglects duties, which constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if it does not constitute a crime, an administrative sanction shall be imposed according to law.

Article 26 The mining license shall be uniformly printed by the competent geology and mineral resources authority under the State Council. The formats of the application registration form, the application form for alteration registration, and the application form for cancellation registration shall be uniformly formulated by the competent geology and mineral resources authority under the State Council.

Article 27 When going through the mining registration formalities, the registration fee shall be paid in accordance with the provisions. The charging standards and the measures for administration and use shall be formulated by the competent price authority under the State Council jointly with the competent geology and mineral resources authority under the State Council and the finance department.

Article 28 The exploitation of mineral resources by foreign investment shall be handled in accordance with the provisions of these Measures; if there are special provisions in other laws or administrative regulations, those provisions shall prevail.

Article 29 Where Chinese and foreign parties cooperate in the exploitation of mineral resources, the Chinese party shall, after signing the contract, file the contract with the original issuing authority for record.

Article 30 For those that have already obtained a mining license before the coming into force of these Measures, the competent geology and mineral resources authority under the State Council shall organize the replacement and issuance of new mining licenses uniformly.
For mining enterprises that have already been established before the coming into force of these Measures, they shall begin to pay the mining right use fee from the date of the coming into force of these Measures, and may apply for reduction or exemption of the fee in accordance with the provisions of these Measures.
Article 31 The registration authority shall announce the mining licenses issued and the mining licenses revoked.

Article 32 For the purpose of these Measures, the term "mining area scope" means the three-dimensional space area of the scope of exploitable mineral resources, the distribution scope of shaft and tunnel engineering facilities, or the scope of open-pit stripping that has been delineated by the registration authority according to law.
For the purpose of these Measures, the term "mining method" means underground mining or open-pit mining.

Article 33 Any amendment to the appendix of these Measures shall be submitted by the competent geology and mineral resources authority under the State Council to the State Council for approval before publication.

Article 34 These Measures shall come into force as of the date of promulgation. The Interim Measures for the Administration of Mining Registration of Mining Enterprises Owned by the Whole People promulgated by the State Council on April 29, 1987, and the Decision of the State Council on Amending the Interim Measures for the Administration of Mining Registration of Mining Enterprises Owned by the Whole People on November 22, 1990, shall be abolished simultaneously.
